question: A community health nurse is counseling a woman who is the head of a family in a village about the eight elements of primary health care. Which element is the MOST appropriate description of education about the prevailing health problems and their prevention?
option_1: Health education about common problems and their prevention
option_2: Supply of essential drugs to the whole village
option_3: Treatment of referred cases in the district hospital
option_4: Provision of safe water to each household at home
solution:
Correct Answer: (a) Health education about common problems and their prevention

Clinical Rationale: Health education about the prevailing problems and their prevention is the stated FIRST element of primary health care.

Key Clue: a woman heading a family in a village

Priority Principle: Primary health care elements

Why Not Others: (b) Essential drugs are supplied but do not give health education; (c) Hospital care is the referral level and not this element; (d) Safe water is a separate element of primary health care.

PGI Exam Trap: Essential drugs are named as the education element.

5-Second Recall: The first element of primary health care is health education.

PNC Exam Pearl: Education about the problem comes before its treatment.

question: A 26-year-old woman visits the clinic and reports that many people in her village have had acute watery stools since a village fair three days ago. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Give each person a long course of antibiotics at home
option_2: Inform the health authorities and begin a rapid search for cases
option_3: Advise the whole village to boil the drinking water
option_4: Wait for the stool culture reports before acting at all
solution:
Correct Answer: (b) Inform the health authorities and begin a rapid search for cases

Clinical Rationale: A cluster of acute watery stools after a gathering points to an outbreak, so the authorities are told and cases are searched for at once.

Key Clue: many people with acute watery stools after a fair

Priority Principle: Suspected outbreak of diarrhoea

Why Not Others: (a) Antibiotics alone do not control an outbreak of diarrhoea; (c) Boiling water helps but is not the very first step; (d) Waiting for the cultures delays the whole outbreak control.

PGI Exam Trap: The nurse waits for the culture reports before acting.

5-Second Recall: Report a cluster and search for cases at once.

PNC Exam Pearl: In an outbreak, act on the signal and confirm later.

question: A 2-year-old child is brought to the clinic for a routine developmental check. Which is the BEST sequence of steps the nurse should follow to screen the development of this child?
option_1: Take the history, give the vaccine, then test the milestones
option_2: Test the milestones FIRST, then greet and take the history
option_3: Greet the child, take the history, observe, then test the milestones
option_4: Observe the child, then weigh, then record the milestones
solution:
Correct Answer: (c) Greet the child, take the history, observe, then test the milestones

Clinical Rationale: A developmental screen begins with a friendly greeting, then the history, then watching the child before the milestones are tested.

Key Clue: a 2-year-old child brought for a routine check

Priority Principle: Developmental screening

Why Not Others: (a) A vaccine is not part of the developmental screening itself; (b) Testing the milestones first frightens the child and gives poor results; (d) Weighing is a growth step and not part of the milestone test.

PGI Exam Trap: The milestones are tested before the child is settled.

5-Second Recall: Settle the child, then screen the milestones.

PNC Exam Pearl: A relaxed child gives a true picture of development.

question: A nurse caring for a family in a village reads the community map that marks every household and the health sub centre. Which interpretation of this map is the MOST appropriate?
option_1: The map lists the families that must be sent to the city
option_2: The map shows the families that have paid a fee for the care
option_3: The map is used to plan the yearly budget of the district
option_4: The marked households show where the families live and where care is planned
solution:
Correct Answer: (d) The marked households show where the families live and where care is planned

Clinical Rationale: A community map marks the homes of the families and the health facility so that nursing care can be planned for the area.

Key Clue: a nurse reading the community map of a village

Priority Principle: Community map reading

Why Not Others: (a) The map does not decide which families go to the city; (b) A community map is not a list of families who have paid; (c) The district budget is planned from other records and not this map.

PGI Exam Trap: The map is read as the district budget plan.

5-Second Recall: The map shows homes and the place of care.

PNC Exam Pearl: A community map guides where the care is taken.

question: A community health nurse visits the home of a family to assess how the family lives and cares for its members. Which reason makes a home visit the MOST appropriate for assessing the health practices of the family?
option_1: The family can avoid coming to the clinic for any care
option_2: The family can be given free medicines during the visit
option_3: The nurse can finish a large number of visits in a short time
option_4: The nurse can see the real living habits of the family as they happen
solution:
Correct Answer: (d) The nurse can see the real living habits of the family as they happen

Clinical Rationale: In the home the nurse sees the family at work and at rest and can judge the true living and health habits of the family.

Key Clue: a nurse visiting the home of a family

Priority Principle: Home visiting

Why Not Others: (a) Home visiting does not stop the family from using the clinic; (b) Free medicines are a service and not the reason for a home visit; (c) Home visits take longer and are not for saving time.

PGI Exam Trap: The home visit is chosen because it saves time.

5-Second Recall: The home shows the real habits of the family.

PNC Exam Pearl: Seeing the family at home tells the truth about their habits.

question: A nurse caring for the families of a village reports a rise in jaundice among those who draw water from one well. Which step is the MOST appropriate to confirm that the well is the source of the infection?
option_1: Send the people affected by jaundice for a liver function test
option_2: Advise the people of the lane to stop using that well at once
option_3: Test the well water and compare it with the stool samples of the cases
option_4: Close the well and arrange a new source of safe water nearby
solution:
Correct Answer: (c) Test the well water and compare it with the stool samples of the cases

Clinical Rationale: To prove that the well is the source, the water is tested and the result is matched with the stool samples of the people who are ill.

Key Clue: a rise in jaundice among those using one well

Priority Principle: Water borne outbreak

Why Not Others: (a) A liver function test is a clinical test and not the water test; (b) Stopping the use of the well is control and not proof; (d) Closing the well is done after the source is confirmed.

PGI Exam Trap: The well is closed before the source is confirmed.

5-Second Recall: Test the water and match it with the cases.

PNC Exam Pearl: The source is proved by the lab, not by guess.

question: A nurse caring for a mother who delivered at home reads that the second postnatal home visit is planned in the sixth to eighth week. Which reason makes this timing the MOST appropriate?
option_1: This is the time when the mother has fully recovered from the delivery
option_2: This is the time to counsel the mother about family planning and the growth of the baby
option_3: This is the time when the baby needs the FIRST dose of a vaccine
option_4: This is the time when the mother can get her iron tablets renewed
solution:
Correct Answer: (b) This is the time to counsel the mother about family planning and the growth of the baby

Clinical Rationale: The sixth to eighth week is chosen so that the mother can be counseled on family planning and on how the baby is growing.

Key Clue: a mother who delivered at home and the second visit date

Priority Principle: Postnatal home visits

Why Not Others: (a) Recovery of the mother is not the reason for this fixed timing; (c) The first vaccine doses come much earlier than this visit; (d) Renewal of iron tablets is not the purpose of this visit.

PGI Exam Trap: The visit is timed for the FIRST vaccine dose.

5-Second Recall: The sixth to eighth week is fixed for counseling.

PNC Exam Pearl: The later postnatal visit is for counseling and growth.

question: A 24-year-old woman in the third trimester comes to the clinic for an antenatal check. Which is the MOST appropriate daily dose of iron and folic acid for the nurse to give her under the national programme?
option_1: One tablet of iron and folic acid every day
option_2: One tablet of iron and folic acid twice a week
option_3: Two tablets of iron and folic acid every week
option_4: One tablet of iron and folic acid every month
solution:
Correct Answer: (a) One tablet of iron and folic acid every day

Clinical Rationale: Under the national programme a pregnant woman takes one tablet of iron and folic acid every day from the second trimester.

Key Clue: a woman in the third trimester at an antenatal check

Priority Principle: Iron and folic acid in pregnancy

Why Not Others: (b) Twice a week is not the daily pregnancy dose; (c) Two tablets a week is far below the daily dose; (d) One tablet a month is the wrong schedule for pregnancy.

PGI Exam Trap: The daily dose is given twice a week.

5-Second Recall: One tablet of iron and folic acid each day.

PNC Exam Pearl: In pregnancy iron and folic acid are taken daily.

question: A nurse caring for the families of a district is asked how the infant mortality rate is worked out. Which statement is the BEST definition of the infant mortality rate?
option_1: Deaths of infants under one year of age per 1000 people in a year
option_2: Deaths of infants under one year of age per 1000 live births in a year
option_3: Deaths of newborns within the FIRST month per 1000 live births
option_4: Deaths of children under five years of age per 1000 live births
solution:
Correct Answer: (b) Deaths of infants under one year of age per 1000 live births in a year

Clinical Rationale: The infant mortality rate counts the deaths of babies under one year in a year for every 1000 live births.

Key Clue: a district and the definition of infant mortality

Priority Principle: Infant mortality rate

Why Not Others: (a) The rate is worked out per 1000 live births and not per people; (c) Deaths in the first month give the neonatal and not the infant rate; (d) Under five deaths give the child mortality and not the infant rate.

PGI Exam Trap: The rate is worked out per 1000 people.

5-Second Recall: Infant deaths under one year per 1000 live births.

PNC Exam Pearl: The working is always per live births, not per people.

question: A 27-year-old woman on the postnatal ward refuses to feed her newborn and says the baby is NOT hers. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Explain to her again and again that the baby is really hers
option_2: Ask the family to feed the baby in place of the mother
option_3: Stay with her and tell the doctor about these thoughts at once
option_4: Leave her alone so that she can settle down with rest
solution:
Correct Answer: (c) Stay with her and tell the doctor about these thoughts at once

Clinical Rationale: Refusing the baby and saying it is NOT hers are danger signs of a puerperal illness, so the nurse stays with her and calls the doctor at once.

Key Clue: a woman on the postnatal ward who refuses her newborn

Priority Principle: Puerperal mood disorder

Why Not Others: (a) Arguing about the baby does not help and may upset her more; (b) Asking the family to feed does not treat the mother's illness; (d) Leaving her alone is unsafe when she has these fixed beliefs.

PGI Exam Trap: The nurse leaves her alone to settle down.

5-Second Recall: Watch her closely and inform the doctor at once.

PNC Exam Pearl: Fixed false beliefs about the baby need urgent care.

question: A nurse caring for the families of a village finds a man and many other adults with breathlessness and swollen ankles who had rheumatic fever as children. Which intervention would have BEST prevented this problem?
option_1: Screening all the adults for heart disease in every year
option_2: Giving every child a monthly injection of long acting penicillin
option_3: Advising the families to keep the children at home in winter
option_4: Prompt treatment of sore throat in children with a full course of penicillin
solution:
Correct Answer: (d) Prompt treatment of sore throat in children with a full course of penicillin

Clinical Rationale: Rheumatic fever follows an untreated sore throat, so prompt and complete penicillin treatment of the throat infection prevents the later valve damage.

Key Clue: many adults with breathlessness and swollen ankles after childhood rheumatic fever

Priority Principle: Rheumatic heart disease

Why Not Others: (a) Screening adults finds the damage but does not prevent it; (b) A monthly injection is for the child who already had rheumatic fever; (c) Keeping children at home does not stop the throat infection.

PGI Exam Trap: The problem is prevented by screening the adults each year.

5-Second Recall: Treat the sore throat fully to prevent rheumatic fever.

PNC Exam Pearl: Prompt throat treatment protects the heart valves.

question: A nurse caring for a child in a village is to conduct a house to house immunisation session for the families there. Which is the BEST order of the steps that the nurse should follow?
option_1: Plan the route, carry the vaccine in a cold box, vaccinate, then record
option_2: Carry the vaccine, plan the route, record the children, then vaccinate
option_3: Vaccinate the children, then plan the route and keep the records
option_4: Record the children, vaccinate them, then carry the cold box
solution:
Correct Answer: (a) Plan the route, carry the vaccine in a cold box, vaccinate, then record

Clinical Rationale: The route is planned FIRST, the vaccine is kept cold, the children are vaccinated, and the records are written at the end.

Key Clue: a house to house immunisation session for the children of a village

Priority Principle: Immunisation session steps

Why Not Others: (b) An unplanned route wastes vaccine and leaves records for later; (c) Vaccinating before planning the route is unsafe and wasteful; (d) The cold box must be carried with the vaccine, not at the end.

PGI Exam Trap: The cold box is carried after the children are vaccinated.

5-Second Recall: Plan, keep cold, vaccinate, then record.

PNC Exam Pearl: The cold chain comes before the children are vaccinated.

question: A nurse caring for the adults of a village arranges screening of a high risk group for the early detection of diabetes. Which is the MOST appropriate level of prevention that the nurse is using here?
option_1: Secondary prevention
option_2: Primary prevention
option_3: Tertiary prevention
option_4: Primordial prevention
solution:
Correct Answer: (a) Secondary prevention

Clinical Rationale: Screening a high risk group to find a disease early is secondary prevention, because the aim is early detection and early treatment.

Key Clue: screening a high risk group for early detection of diabetes

Priority Principle: Levels of prevention

Why Not Others: (b) Primary prevention stops the disease before it starts; (c) Tertiary prevention limits disability after the disease; (d) Primordial prevention targets the whole population and its habits.

PGI Exam Trap: Early detection is called primary prevention.

5-Second Recall: Early detection by screening is secondary prevention.

PNC Exam Pearl: Finding a disease early belongs to secondary prevention.

question: A nurse caring for the families of four villages notes that the sub centre covers a total population of 5200 people. About how many households does the sub centre cover if the average household has five members? Which value is MOST appropriate?
option_1: About 1300 households
option_2: About 520 households
option_3: About 2600 households
option_4: About 1040 households
solution:
Correct Answer: (d) About 1040 households

Clinical Rationale: The number of households is found by dividing the total population by the average size of the household, so 5200 divided by 5 is about 1040.

Key Clue: a sub centre covering 5200 people with five members to a household

Priority Principle: Community statistics

Why Not Others: (a) Dividing by four is not the average household size here; (b) Dividing by ten rather than by five gives the wrong figure; (c) Multiplying by two rather than dividing gives the wrong figure.

PGI Exam Trap: The population is multiplied instead of divided.

5-Second Recall: Divide the population by the household size.

PNC Exam Pearl: Households equal people divided by the family size.

question: A nurse caring for a family in a village is asked why the sub centre registers are written up at every contact instead of once a month. Which reason is the MOST appropriate?
option_1: Writing the register once a month takes far too much time
option_2: The register is checked by the doctor every single day
option_3: Care given at each contact is written down at once so that no case is missed
option_4: The monthly report is sent to the district office in the city
solution:
Correct Answer: (c) Care given at each contact is written down at once so that no case is missed

Clinical Rationale: Writing up the register at every contact keeps the record of care current, so that no case is lost between the monthly reports.

Key Clue: a sub centre register written at every contact

Priority Principle: Record keeping

Why Not Others: (a) Once a month takes less time and this is not the reason; (b) The doctor does not check the register every single day; (d) The monthly report is a separate duty and not the reason.

PGI Exam Trap: The register is kept only to prepare the monthly report.

5-Second Recall: Write the register at each contact.

PNC Exam Pearl: A current record keeps the care on track.

question: A 30-year-old man comes to the clinic and reports that four people in his street have become yellow and unwell in the past week. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Advise the family to rest and take only light food
option_2: Visit the street and search for more cases among the neighbours
option_3: Send the man to the district hospital that very day
option_4: Wait for a laboratory report before doing anything
solution:
Correct Answer: (b) Visit the street and search for more cases among the neighbours

Clinical Rationale: A cluster of jaundice in one street suggests an outbreak, so the nurse visits the street and looks for more cases at once.

Key Clue: four people in one street who have become yellow

Priority Principle: Suspected hepatitis outbreak

Why Not Others: (a) Rest and light food are supportive and not the first step; (c) Sending the man away delays the search for other cases; (d) Waiting for the report lets the outbreak spread further.

PGI Exam Trap: The nurse waits for the laboratory report before acting.

5-Second Recall: Search the street for more cases at once.

PNC Exam Pearl: In an outbreak the search comes before the lab.

question: A nurse caring for a child at the anganwadi sees a growth chart of a 2-year-old whose weight line has fallen across two zones in three months. Which interpretation of this chart is the MOST appropriate?
option_1: The child is NOT gaining weight well and needs feeding advice and follow up
option_2: The child is healthy and no further action is needed now
option_3: The chart is wrong and should be started again from the top
option_4: The child can be sent home and seen again after a year
solution:
Correct Answer: (a) The child is NOT gaining weight well and needs feeding advice and follow up

Clinical Rationale: A weight line that falls across two zones shows that the child is NOT growing well, so feeding advice and close follow up are needed.

Key Clue: a weight line falling across two zones in a child

Priority Principle: Growth monitoring

Why Not Others: (b) A fall across two zones is not a healthy weight line; (c) The chart record is not wrong because the line is falling; (d) A review after a year is far too late for this child.

PGI Exam Trap: The child is sent home and reviewed after a year.

5-Second Recall: A fall across two zones needs feeding advice.

PNC Exam Pearl: A falling weight line is an early warning.

question: A nurse caring for a family in a village explains why the oral polio vaccine is given in extra rounds during the pulse polio campaign. Which reason is the MOST appropriate?
option_1: The extra rounds are held for the school children
option_2: A single round of the vaccine does NOT work in any child
option_3: The vaccine is never given during the routine sessions
option_4: Extra rounds reach every child and keep the virus out of the community
solution:
Correct Answer: (d) Extra rounds reach every child and keep the virus out of the community

Clinical Rationale: Extra rounds cover the children who were missed in the routine sessions, so the polio virus is kept out of the whole community.

Key Clue: extra rounds of the oral polio vaccine in a campaign

Priority Principle: Pulse polio campaign

Why Not Others: (a) The rounds cover all young children and not only school children; (b) A single round does work, but it may miss some children; (c) The vaccine is also given in the routine sessions.

PGI Exam Trap: The vaccine is meant only for school children.

5-Second Recall: Extra rounds reach the children who were missed.

PNC Exam Pearl: Every missed child keeps the virus alive.

Reference Table: Normal adult vital signs - Temperature: 36.1-37.2 C (97-99 F); Pulse: 60-100 /min; Respiration: 12-20 /min; Blood pressure: < 120/80 mmHg; SpO2: 95-100% (COPD target 88-92%).

question: A nurse caring for a man on treatment for tuberculosis explains why three antitubercular drugs are given together every day. Which reason is the MOST appropriate?
option_1: The three drugs shorten the treatment to a few weeks only
option_2: Each drug works alone and the others are given for the fever
option_3: The three drugs together kill the bacteria and stop drug resistance
option_4: The drugs are given together to reduce the daily cost
solution:
Correct Answer: (c) The three drugs together kill the bacteria and stop drug resistance

Clinical Rationale: A combination of drugs is used from the start so that the bacteria are killed and the germ does NOT become resistant to any one drug.

Key Clue: three antitubercular drugs given together every day

Priority Principle: Antitubercular therapy

Why Not Others: (a) The full course still lasts several months, not weeks; (b) The drugs work together and none is given for fever; (d) Cost is not the reason for combining the drugs.

PGI Exam Trap: One drug is enough at the start of the treatment.

5-Second Recall: A combination prevents drug resistance.

PNC Exam Pearl: Combining drugs protects the cure.

Reference Table: Normal adult vital signs - Temperature: 36.1-37.2 C (97-99 F); Pulse: 60-100 /min; Respiration: 12-20 /min; Blood pressure: < 120/80 mmHg; SpO2: 95-100% (COPD target 88-92%).

question: A nurse caring for a family in a district is asked which indicator is the MOST appropriate to measure the immunisation coverage of the district.
option_1: The number of vaccine vials used in the district
option_2: The proportion of children fully immunised for their age
option_3: The number of immunisation sessions held in a month
option_4: The amount of money spent on the vaccines
solution:
Correct Answer: (b) The proportion of children fully immunised for their age

Clinical Rationale: Immunisation coverage is measured by the share of children who have received all the vaccines due for their age.

Key Clue: measuring the immunisation coverage of a district

Priority Principle: Immunisation coverage

Why Not Others: (a) Vials used do not show how many children were covered; (c) More sessions do not promise full coverage of children; (d) The cost does not measure how many children were immunised.

PGI Exam Trap: Vials used are taken as the coverage indicator.

5-Second Recall: Coverage is the share of children fully immunised.

PNC Exam Pearl: Count the children, not the vials.

question: A nurse caring for a child in a village is to do a rapid fever survey for malaria during an outbreak. Which is the BEST order of the steps that the nurse should follow?
option_1: Take the smears, then plan, then search for fever cases
option_2: Give the treatment, then find the cases and take smears
option_3: Find the fever cases, take a blood smear, then give the treatment
option_4: Spray the houses, then find the cases and treat them
solution:
Correct Answer: (c) Find the fever cases, take a blood smear, then give the treatment

Clinical Rationale: A rapid fever survey finds the fever cases FIRST, takes a blood smear to confirm malaria, and then starts the treatment.

Key Clue: a rapid fever survey for malaria in a village

Priority Principle: Fever survey steps

Why Not Others: (a) The survey cannot be planned after the smears are taken; (b) Treating before the smear is taken loses the chance to confirm; (d) Spraying is vector control and comes after the survey.

PGI Exam Trap: The treatment is started before the smear is taken.

5-Second Recall: Find the cases, smear, then treat.

PNC Exam Pearl: Confirm the fever before treating it.

Reference Table: Normal adult vital signs - Temperature: 36.1-37.2 C (97-99 F); Pulse: 60-100 /min; Respiration: 12-20 /min; Blood pressure: < 120/80 mmHg; SpO2: 95-100% (COPD target 88-92%).

question: A nurse caring for a family reads that the family folder marks an elderly member who is disabled. Which use of this record is the MOST appropriate?
option_1: It shows that the family does NOT need any nursing care
option_2: It reminds the nurse to plan care and follow up for that member
option_3: It is kept so that the family can be charged for the care
option_4: It is written to complete the yearly report of the area
solution:
Correct Answer: (b) It reminds the nurse to plan care and follow up for that member

Clinical Rationale: A family folder that marks a disabled elderly member guides the nurse to plan and follow up the care that this member needs.

Key Clue: a family folder marking a disabled elderly member

Priority Principle: Family folder

Why Not Others: (a) The mark shows a need for care and not the absence of it; (c) The folder is a care record and not a bill for the family; (d) The report is a by-product and not the main use of the record.

PGI Exam Trap: The mark means that the family needs no care.

5-Second Recall: The folder guides care and follow up.

PNC Exam Pearl: A care record plans the next visit.

question: A nurse caring for a high risk pregnant woman in a village arranges her referral to the hospital. Which is the BEST order of the steps that the nurse should follow?
option_1: Find the danger sign, inform the family, arrange transport, then send her
option_2: Send her to the hospital, then inform the family later
option_3: Wait for the next clinic day and then refer her to a doctor
option_4: Give her medicines and ask her to return if she feels worse
solution:
Correct Answer: (a) Find the danger sign, inform the family, arrange transport, then send her

Clinical Rationale: Referral of a high risk woman means finding the danger sign, informing the family, arranging transport and then sending her without delay.

Key Clue: the referral of a high risk pregnant woman

Priority Principle: Referral steps

Why Not Others: (b) The family must be told before the woman is sent away; (c) Waiting for the clinic day wastes precious time; (d) Medicines alone do not treat the high risk condition.

PGI Exam Trap: The woman is sent away before the family is told.

5-Second Recall: Inform the family and arrange transport.

PNC Exam Pearl: A high risk referral must not wait.

question: A nurse caring for an antenatal woman explains the pattern of the four antenatal visits under the national programme. Which pattern is the MOST appropriate?
option_1: One visit in each trimester of the pregnancy
option_2: One visit in each month from the FIRST to the ninth
option_3: Two visits in each month of the last trimester
option_4: One visit each in the FIRST, third, sixth and ninth months
solution:
Correct Answer: (d) One visit each in the FIRST, third, sixth and ninth months

Clinical Rationale: The national programme advises four antenatal visits, one each in the FIRST, third, sixth and ninth months of the pregnancy.

Key Clue: the four antenatal visits under the national programme

Priority Principle: Antenatal visit schedule

Why Not Others: (a) One visit in each trimester gives only three visits; (b) A visit every month is more than the four visits advised; (c) Two visits a month in the last trimester is not this pattern.

PGI Exam Trap: One visit in each trimester gives the four visits.

5-Second Recall: Four visits in the 1st, 3rd, 6th and 9th months.

PNC Exam Pearl: Four visits are spaced through the pregnancy.

question: A nurse caring for a family in a village is asked which part of a community diagnosis describes the demography of the area. Which description is the MOST appropriate?
option_1: The sources of water and the places of waste
option_2: The number of clinics and their working hours
option_3: The beliefs and customs of the people of the area
option_4: The number of people, their age groups and their sex
solution:
Correct Answer: (d) The number of people, their age groups and their sex

Clinical Rationale: Demography describes the people themselves, so it gives their number, their age groups and their sex.

Key Clue: the demography part of a community diagnosis

Priority Principle: Demography

Why Not Others: (a) Water and waste belong to the environmental part; (b) Clinics and their timings belong to the health services; (c) Beliefs and customs belong to the social and cultural part.

PGI Exam Trap: The number of clinics is the demography of the area.

5-Second Recall: Demography is the people and their age and sex.

PNC Exam Pearl: Demography counts the people, not the clinics.

question: A 22-year-old man comes to the clinic with pain in the abdomen that began near the navel and settled in the right lower part. Which site is the MOST appropriate to test for tenderness in acute appendicitis?
option_1: The epigastric region below the ribs
option_2: The left iliac fossa near the groin
option_3: McBurney point in the right iliac fossa
option_4: The right hypochondrium under the liver
solution:
Correct Answer: (c) McBurney point in the right iliac fossa

Clinical Rationale: Pain that shifts from the navel to the right lower abdomen points to appendicitis, and tenderness is tested at McBurney point.

Key Clue: pain shifting to the right lower abdomen

Priority Principle: Acute appendicitis

Why Not Others: (a) The epigastric region is where the pain often begins; (b) The left iliac fossa is not the site of the appendix; (d) The right hypochondrium lies under the liver.

PGI Exam Trap: The left iliac fossa is tested for appendicitis.

5-Second Recall: McBurney point shows appendicitis.

PNC Exam Pearl: The appendix sits low on the right side.

question: A nurse caring for a mother who will deliver at home explains why hand washing with soap is given the highest importance before the delivery. Which reason is the MOST appropriate?
option_1: It keeps the hands clean and warm for the delivery work
option_2: It removes the germs from the hands and prevents infection in the mother and baby
option_3: It is a custom that the family expects the nurse to follow
option_4: It saves the time needed to clean the room afterwards
solution:
Correct Answer: (b) It removes the germs from the hands and prevents infection in the mother and baby

Clinical Rationale: Hand washing with soap removes the germs on the hands and so prevents infection in the mother and the newborn during a home delivery.

Key Clue: hand washing before a home delivery

Priority Principle: Asepsis at delivery

Why Not Others: (a) Warmth is not the aim of washing the hands with soap; (c) Hand washing is done for safety and not as a custom; (d) Cleaning the room later is not the reason for hand washing.

PGI Exam Trap: Hand washing is done to keep the hands warm.

5-Second Recall: Soap removes germs and prevents infection.

PNC Exam Pearl: Clean hands protect mother and baby.

question: A mother at home tells the health worker that her child has had loose stools since morning and is drinking well. Which advice should the nurse give FIRST?
option_1: Give extra fluid with oral rehydration salts at home and continue feeding
option_2: Stop all food and give plain water for the whole day
option_3: Bring the child to the clinic at once for an injection
option_4: Give a home remedy and review the child after three days
solution:
Correct Answer: (a) Give extra fluid with oral rehydration salts at home and continue feeding

Clinical Rationale: A child with loose stools who is still drinking is NOT dehydrated, so the FIRST advice is extra fluid with oral rehydration salts and continued feeding.

Key Clue: a child with loose stools who is drinking well

Priority Principle: Diarrhoea at home

Why Not Others: (b) Stopping the food delays recovery and weakens the child; (c) An injection is not needed when the child is drinking well; (d) A review after three days is too late if the stools continue.

PGI Exam Trap: The child is sent to the clinic for an injection.

5-Second Recall: Give oral rehydration fluid and continue feeding.

PNC Exam Pearl: A drinking child is managed at home.

question: A 40-year-old man visits the clinic and reports increased thirst, passing urine often and loss of weight over three months. Which investigation should the nurse arrange FIRST?
option_1: An x ray film of the chest
option_2: A urine test for albumin in the sample
option_3: A blood test for the level of cholesterol
option_4: A blood sugar test taken after fasting
solution:
Correct Answer: (d) A blood sugar test taken after fasting

Clinical Rationale: Thirst, frequent passing of urine and loss of weight point to diabetes, so the FIRST investigation is a fasting blood sugar test.

Key Clue: thirst, frequent urine and weight loss in a man

Priority Principle: Diabetes mellitus

Why Not Others: (a) A chest film is done for the lungs and not the sugar; (b) Albumin in the urine tests the kidney and not the sugar; (c) Cholesterol is tested for the heart and not for diabetes.

PGI Exam Trap: A chest film is taken FIRST to find diabetes.

5-Second Recall: A fasting blood sugar test comes first.

PNC Exam Pearl: Thirst and weight loss point to sugar.

question: A nurse caring for a family in a village is asked which model explains a disease as the interaction of the agent, the host and the environment. Which model is the MOST appropriate?
option_1: The epidemiological triad
option_2: The health belief model
option_3: The web of causation
option_4: The levels of prevention
solution:
Correct Answer: (a) The epidemiological triad

Clinical Rationale: The epidemiological triad explains a disease as the result of the interaction between the agent, the host and the environment.

Key Clue: the agent, the host and the environment

Priority Principle: Epidemiological triad

Why Not Others: (b) The health belief model explains the health behaviour of people; (c) The web of causation shows many factors acting together; (d) The levels of prevention describe stages of prevention.

PGI Exam Trap: The web of causation names only the three factors.

5-Second Recall: Agent, host and environment make the triad.

PNC Exam Pearl: The triad links germ, person and place.

question: A 45-year-old man comes to the clinic with a cough for three weeks and an evening rise of temperature. Which action should the nurse take FIRST under the national programme?
option_1: Give him a course of cough syrup and send him home
option_2: Collect two sputum samples and send them for the test
option_3: Ask him to come back if the cough becomes worse
option_4: Take an x ray film of the chest in the clinic itself
solution:
Correct Answer: (b) Collect two sputum samples and send them for the test

Clinical Rationale: A cough for more than two weeks with evening fever is a suspected case of tuberculosis, so two sputum samples are collected and sent for testing.

Key Clue: a cough for three weeks with evening fever

Priority Principle: Suspected tuberculosis

Why Not Others: (a) Cough syrup does not treat tuberculosis and delays the test; (c) Asking him to return delays the diagnosis of tuberculosis; (d) The sputum test comes before any chest film is taken.

PGI Exam Trap: The chest film is taken before the sputum test.

5-Second Recall: Collect two sputum samples and test them.

PNC Exam Pearl: A long cough with evening fever needs a sputum test.

Reference Table: Normal adult vital signs - Temperature: 36.1-37.2 C (97-99 F); Pulse: 60-100 /min; Respiration: 12-20 /min; Blood pressure: < 120/80 mmHg; SpO2: 95-100% (COPD target 88-92%).

question: A nurse caring for a family in a village explains why a sanitary latrine is emphasised in a village sanitation programme. Which reason is the MOST appropriate?
option_1: It is required by the law for every village household
option_2: It keeps the village neat and pleasant to look at
option_3: It keeps the stools away from people and stops the spread of infection
option_4: It saves the family the trouble of going out at night
solution:
Correct Answer: (c) It keeps the stools away from people and stops the spread of infection

Clinical Rationale: A sanitary latrine keeps the human stools away from the people, the water and the food, and so stops the spread of infection.

Key Clue: a sanitary latrine in a village sanitation programme

Priority Principle: Sanitation

Why Not Others: (a) The law is not the health reason for the latrine; (b) Neatness is a benefit but not the health reason; (d) Convenience is not the reason for the programme.

PGI Exam Trap: The latrine is built only to keep the village neat.

5-Second Recall: The latrine keeps the stools from the people.

PNC Exam Pearl: Safe disposal of stools stops infection.

question: A nurse caring for a man at the clinic explains which test is used for the FIRST screening of a blood sample for HIV under the national programme. Which test is the MOST appropriate?
option_1: The test for the CD4 cell count
option_2: The rapid test for HIV antibodies
option_3: The western blot test
option_4: The test for the viral load
solution:
Correct Answer: (b) The rapid test for HIV antibodies

Clinical Rationale: The FIRST screening test for HIV under the national programme is the rapid test for the HIV antibodies in the blood.

Key Clue: the FIRST screening test for HIV in a blood sample

Priority Principle: HIV testing

Why Not Others: (a) The CD4 count measures the damage and is not the first screen; (c) The western blot is a confirmatory test and not the first; (d) The viral load measures the virus and is not the screen.

PGI Exam Trap: The western blot test is used as the FIRST screen.

5-Second Recall: The rapid antibody test is the first screen.

PNC Exam Pearl: Screen with the rapid test, confirm later.

question: A nurse caring for a family at the primary health centre explains why the ice lined refrigerator is kept in the cold chain. Which reason is the MOST appropriate?
option_1: It stores the medicines of the whole health centre
option_2: It freezes the vaccines so that they last much longer
option_3: It keeps the vaccines cool and safe from heat and from freezing
option_4: It is used to keep the drinking water cool for the staff
solution:
Correct Answer: (c) It keeps the vaccines cool and safe from heat and from freezing

Clinical Rationale: The ice lined refrigerator holds the vaccine at a cool temperature and protects it both from heat and from freezing.

Key Clue: the ice lined refrigerator in the cold chain

Priority Principle: Cold chain

Why Not Others: (a) The refrigerator is for the vaccines and not the medicines; (b) Freezing damages some vaccines and is not the purpose; (d) Drinking water is not stored in this refrigerator.

PGI Exam Trap: The refrigerator is used to freeze the vaccines.

5-Second Recall: It keeps the vaccine cool without freezing.

PNC Exam Pearl: The cold chain protects the vaccine from heat.

Reference Table: Normal adult vital signs - Temperature: 36.1-37.2 C (97-99 F); Pulse: 60-100 /min; Respiration: 12-20 /min; Blood pressure: < 120/80 mmHg; SpO2: 95-100% (COPD target 88-92%).

question: A nurse caring for a child at the anganwadi explains why the weight of the child is plotted on the growth chart at every visit. Which reason is the MOST appropriate?
option_1: The chart is used to decide the next dose of a vaccine
option_2: The chart shows the exact age of the child in months
option_3: The weight is written to complete the anganwadi register
option_4: The line shows whether the child is growing well over the months
solution:
Correct Answer: (d) The line shows whether the child is growing well over the months

Clinical Rationale: Plotting the weight at every visit joins the dots into a line that shows whether the child is growing well month after month.

Key Clue: plotting the weight of a child on the growth chart

Priority Principle: Growth monitoring

Why Not Others: (a) The chart is for growth and not for the vaccine dose; (b) The age is written on the card and is not shown by the line; (c) The register is a record and not the reason to plot.

PGI Exam Trap: The line is plotted to complete the register.

5-Second Recall: The line shows the growth over the months.

PNC Exam Pearl: A line of weights tells how the child grows.

question: A nurse caring for a family in a village is asked how the under five mortality rate is worked out. Which statement is the BEST definition of the under five mortality rate?
option_1: Deaths of children under five years per 1000 live births in a year
option_2: Deaths of children under five years per 1000 people in a year
option_3: Deaths of infants under one year per 1000 live births
option_4: Deaths of children between one and five years per 1000 births
solution:
Correct Answer: (a) Deaths of children under five years per 1000 live births in a year

Clinical Rationale: The under five mortality rate counts the deaths of children below five years in a year for every 1000 live births.

Key Clue: the working out of the under five mortality rate

Priority Principle: Under five mortality rate

Why Not Others: (b) The rate is worked out per 1000 live births and not per people; (c) Infants under one year give the infant mortality rate; (d) Children of one to five years are not the whole under five group.

PGI Exam Trap: The rate is worked out per 1000 people.

5-Second Recall: Under five deaths per 1000 live births.

PNC Exam Pearl: The bottom of the working is always live births.

question: A nurse caring for a family in a village notes that the village has a population of 4000 people and 120 live births in a year. Which value is the MOST appropriate birth rate of the village?
option_1: 40 per 1000 population
option_2: 33 per 1000 population
option_3: 12 per 1000 population
option_4: 30 per 1000 population
solution:
Correct Answer: (d) 30 per 1000 population

Clinical Rationale: The birth rate is the live births in a year for every 1000 people, so 120 births in a population of 4000 gives a rate of 30.

Key Clue: a population of 4000 and 120 live births

Priority Principle: Birth rate

Why Not Others: (a) A rate of 40 is far too high for these figures; (b) Dividing 120 by 3600 gives the wrong figure; (c) Dividing by ten gives the wrong figure here.

PGI Exam Trap: The births are divided by ten to get the rate.

5-Second Recall: Live births per 1000 people in a year.

PNC Exam Pearl: Divide the births, multiply by a thousand.

question: A nurse caring for a 2-year-old child at the sub centre explains why co-trimoxazole is given for the fast breathing and the fever. Which reason is the MOST appropriate?
option_1: It treats the pneumonia that causes the fast breathing and the fever
option_2: It brings down the fever and has no effect on the breathing
option_3: It prevents the child from getting a cough in the future
option_4: It is given to every child who comes to the sub centre
solution:
Correct Answer: (a) It treats the pneumonia that causes the fast breathing and the fever

Clinical Rationale: Fast breathing with fever in a young child is treated as pneumonia, so co-trimoxazole is given to treat the infection that causes both signs.

Key Clue: a 2-year-old child with fast breathing and fever

Priority Principle: Childhood pneumonia

Why Not Others: (b) The drug treats the infection and does work on the breathing; (c) It is not given to prevent a future cough; (d) It is given only to the children with these signs.

PGI Exam Trap: The drug is given to every child at the centre.

5-Second Recall: It treats the pneumonia behind the signs.

PNC Exam Pearl: Fast breathing with fever means pneumonia.

Reference Table: Normal adult vital signs - Temperature: 36.1-37.2 C (97-99 F); Pulse: 60-100 /min; Respiration: 12-20 /min; Blood pressure: < 120/80 mmHg; SpO2: 95-100% (COPD target 88-92%).

question: A nurse caring for an antenatal woman reads that the antenatal card at 36 weeks shows a fundal height smaller than the period of gestation on two visits. Which interpretation of this card is the MOST appropriate?
option_1: The dates of the pregnancy are surely wrong here
option_2: The baby may be growing poorly and needs further assessment
option_3: The card is filled in wrongly and should be done again
option_4: The baby is small but needs no further test at all
solution:
Correct Answer: (b) The baby may be growing poorly and needs further assessment

Clinical Rationale: A fundal height that stays smaller than the period of gestation on two visits points to poor growth, so the baby needs further assessment.

Key Clue: a fundal height smaller than the period of gestation

Priority Principle: Poor fetal growth

Why Not Others: (a) Wrong dates are possible, but two small readings need a check; (c) The card is not the problem when the readings stay small; (d) A baby who is small does need further assessment.

PGI Exam Trap: A small baby needs no further test at all.

5-Second Recall: Two small readings need further assessment.

PNC Exam Pearl: Check the growth when the height lags behind.

question: A nurse caring for a family in a village is asked which statement is the BEST definition of a community in community health nursing practice.
option_1: The families that live together in one street of the village
option_2: All the people who attend the same health clinic regularly
option_3: A group of people living in a defined area with common interests and needs
option_4: The people who work together in the same office or factory
solution:
Correct Answer: (c) A group of people living in a defined area with common interests and needs

Clinical Rationale: In community health nursing a community is a group of people who live in a defined area and share common interests and needs.

Key Clue: the definition of a community in nursing practice

Priority Principle: Community

Why Not Others: (a) One street is a part of a community and not the whole; (b) People who attend one clinic may live in many areas; (d) Workmates share a place of work and not a home area.

PGI Exam Trap: One street of a village is the whole community.

5-Second Recall: A community is people with common needs.

PNC Exam Pearl: A community shares a place and interests.

question: A 30-year-old man comes to the clinic after two episodes of an elated mood with reduced sleep and overactivity, with periods of low mood between them. Which condition is the MOST appropriate explanation of this pattern?
option_1: Schizophrenia
option_2: Bipolar affective disorder
option_3: Generalised anxiety disorder
option_4: Recurrent depressive disorder
solution:
Correct Answer: (b) Bipolar affective disorder

Clinical Rationale: Episodes of an elated mood with overactivity that alternate with periods of low mood are the pattern of bipolar affective disorder.

Key Clue: elated mood with overactivity and periods of low mood

Priority Principle: Bipolar affective disorder

Why Not Others: (a) Schizophrenia shows odd beliefs and not clear mood swings; (c) Anxiety gives worry and fear without these mood swings; (d) Depressive disorder gives low mood only and no elated phase.

PGI Exam Trap: The pattern is called recurrent depressive disorder.

5-Second Recall: High and low moods together mean bipolar disorder.

PNC Exam Pearl: Two poles of mood point to bipolar illness.

question: A nurse caring for a family in a district notes 60 maternal deaths and 60000 live births in a year. Which is the MOST appropriate maternal mortality ratio of the district?
option_1: 100 per 100000 live births
option_2: 10 per 100000 live births
option_3: 1000 per 100000 live births
option_4: 1 per 1000 live births
solution:
Correct Answer: (a) 100 per 100000 live births

Clinical Rationale: The maternal mortality ratio is the maternal deaths in a year for every 100000 live births, so 60 deaths in 60000 births gives 100.

Key Clue: 60 maternal deaths and 60000 live births

Priority Principle: Maternal mortality ratio

Why Not Others: (b) A figure of 10 is ten times too small for these numbers; (c) A figure of 1000 is ten times too high for these numbers; (d) One per 1000 births is far too low for these numbers.

PGI Exam Trap: The deaths are divided by a hundred to get the ratio.

5-Second Recall: Maternal deaths per 100000 live births.

PNC Exam Pearl: The ratio counts deaths among live births.

question: A nurse caring for a family in a village is to use the bag technique during a home visit. Which is the BEST order of the steps that the nurse should follow?
option_1: Open the bag on the floor and then take out the articles
option_2: Take out the articles FIRST, then wash the hands and open the bag
option_3: Wash the hands, then place the bag on the bed and open it
option_4: Place the bag on a clean paper, wash the hands, then take out the articles
solution:
Correct Answer: (d) Place the bag on a clean paper, wash the hands, then take out the articles

Clinical Rationale: In the bag technique the bag is placed on a clean sheet of paper, the hands are washed, and only then are the articles taken out.

Key Clue: the bag technique during a home visit

Priority Principle: Bag technique

Why Not Others: (a) The bag is never opened on the floor of the house; (b) Articles are not taken out before the hands are washed; (c) The bag is not placed on the bed of the family.

PGI Exam Trap: The bag is opened on the floor of the house.

5-Second Recall: Clean paper, washed hands, then the articles.

PNC Exam Pearl: The bag stays off the floor and the hands stay clean.

question: A nurse caring for the family of a man on treatment for leprosy explains which drug may be given as a single dose to the close contacts. Which drug is the MOST appropriate?
option_1: Clofazimine as a single dose
option_2: Dapsone as a single dose
option_3: Rifampicin as a single dose
option_4: Isoniazid as a single dose
solution:
Correct Answer: (c) Rifampicin as a single dose

Clinical Rationale: A single dose of rifampicin is given as chemoprophylaxis to the close contacts of a case of leprosy when it is advised.

Key Clue: a single dose of a drug for the contacts of leprosy

Priority Principle: Leprosy chemoprophylaxis

Why Not Others: (a) Clofazimine is part of the course and not the single dose; (b) Dapsone is given in the regular course and not as this dose; (d) Isoniazid is given for tuberculosis and not for leprosy.

PGI Exam Trap: Isoniazid is given to the contacts of leprosy.

5-Second Recall: Rifampicin as a single dose for contacts.

PNC Exam Pearl: One dose of rifampicin protects the contacts.

question: A nurse caring for a family in a village is asked which services are given at the anganwadi centre under the integrated child development scheme. Which service is the MOST appropriate?
option_1: Supplementary nutrition, pre school education and a health check up
option_2: Free medicines and surgery for the village children
option_3: Antenatal care for the mothers of the whole village
option_4: Immunisation of the infants of the whole village
solution:
Correct Answer: (a) Supplementary nutrition, pre school education and a health check up

Clinical Rationale: The anganwadi centre gives supplementary nutrition, pre school education and a health check up to the young children of the area.

Key Clue: the services of the anganwadi centre

Priority Principle: Integrated child development scheme

Why Not Others: (b) Surgery is done in hospital and not at the anganwadi; (c) Antenatal care is given at the sub centre and not here; (d) Immunisation is given at the sessions and not at the anganwadi.

PGI Exam Trap: Surgery for the children is done at the anganwadi.

5-Second Recall: Nutrition, pre school and a health check up.

PNC Exam Pearl: The anganwadi feeds, teaches and checks the child.

question: A nurse caring for a woman after delivery reads that she has a second degree perineal tear. Which description of this tear is the MOST appropriate?
option_1: It involves the perineal skin alone and is a very small tear
option_2: It involves the perineal skin and the muscles, but NOT the anal sphincter
option_3: It extends into the anal sphincter and into the rectum as well
option_4: It lies inside the birth canal and NOT on the outside at all
solution:
Correct Answer: (b) It involves the perineal skin and the muscles, but NOT the anal sphincter

Clinical Rationale: A second degree perineal tear goes through the perineal skin and the perineal muscles, but it spares the anal sphincter.

Key Clue: a second degree perineal tear after delivery

Priority Principle: Perineal tear

Why Not Others: (a) A tear of the skin alone is a first degree tear; (c) A tear into the sphincter and rectum is a fourth degree tear; (d) A perineal tear is on the outside and not inside the canal.

PGI Exam Trap: The skin tear alone is called the second degree.

5-Second Recall: Skin and muscle but not the sphincter.

PNC Exam Pearl: Second degree spares the sphincter.

question: A nurse caring for an elderly man on a home visit finds bruises on his arms and his family prevents him from meeting anyone. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Ask him to come to the clinic on the next clinic day
option_2: Advise the family to look after him with much more care
option_3: Report the matter to the authorities and arrange his safety at once
option_4: Note the bruises in the register and visit him again later
solution:
Correct Answer: (c) Report the matter to the authorities and arrange his safety at once

Clinical Rationale: Bruises with a family that keeps an elderly man away from others is a sign of abuse, so the nurse reports it and arranges his safety at once.

Key Clue: an elderly man with bruises kept away from others

Priority Principle: Elder abuse

Why Not Others: (a) Asking him to come to the clinic leaves him in danger; (b) Advice to the family does not keep the man safe now; (d) Writing in the register does not protect him today.

PGI Exam Trap: The nurse writes the bruises in the register and goes away.

5-Second Recall: Report and make him safe at once.

PNC Exam Pearl: Bruises and isolation are signs of abuse.

question: A nurse caring for a family in a village is to test the household salt for iodine. Which is the BEST order of the steps that the nurse should follow?
option_1: Mix the salt with water, then add the solution to it
option_2: Read the colour FIRST, then put the solution on the salt
option_3: Taste the salt FIRST, then add the solution and read it
option_4: Put a drop of the test solution on the salt, then read the colour
solution:
Correct Answer: (d) Put a drop of the test solution on the salt, then read the colour

Clinical Rationale: To test the salt for iodine, a drop of the test solution is put on the salt and the colour that appears is read.

Key Clue: testing the household salt for iodine

Priority Principle: Iodised salt test

Why Not Others: (a) Watering the salt spoils the simple colour test; (b) The colour is read after the solution is added, not before; (c) Tasting the salt is not part of this test.

PGI Exam Trap: The colour is read before the solution is added.

5-Second Recall: Add the solution, then read the colour.

PNC Exam Pearl: A drop of solution shows the iodine by colour.

question: A 22-year-old man is brought to the sub centre by his family because he has strange beliefs and talks to himself. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Give him a sedative injection and let him sleep for a while
option_2: Tell the family that he is only acting and send him home
option_3: Assess him for any danger to himself and arrange a psychiatric referral
option_4: Advise the family to take him to a temple for special prayers
solution:
Correct Answer: (c) Assess him for any danger to himself and arrange a psychiatric referral

Clinical Rationale: Strange beliefs with self talk point to a mental illness, so the nurse FIRST checks for any danger to himself and then arranges a psychiatric referral.

Key Clue: strange beliefs and talking to himself in a young man

Priority Principle: Psychiatric referral

Why Not Others: (a) A sedative settles him for a time but is not the first step; (b) The man needs care and is not simply acting; (d) Prayers do not treat a mental illness that needs care.

PGI Exam Trap: The man is sent home and told that he is acting.

5-Second Recall: Check for danger, then refer him.

PNC Exam Pearl: Self talk with odd beliefs needs psychiatric care.

question: A 35-year-old man who works on a farm comes to the clinic with a deep foot wound that is dirty with soil, and he has never been vaccinated against tetanus. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Dress the wound and ask him to come back after a week
option_2: Clean the wound and give the tetanus vaccine with the immunoglobulin
option_3: Give him a dose of the tetanus vaccine and nothing else
option_4: Wash the wound and give an antibiotic tablet by mouth
solution:
Correct Answer: (b) Clean the wound and give the tetanus vaccine with the immunoglobulin

Clinical Rationale: A deep wound dirty with soil in an unvaccinated man carries a high risk of tetanus, so the wound is cleaned and both the vaccine and the immunoglobulin are given.

Key Clue: a deep soiled wound in a man never given tetanus vaccine

Priority Principle: Tetanus prophylaxis

Why Not Others: (a) A dressing alone leaves the man at risk of tetanus; (c) The vaccine is needed with the immunoglobulin here; (d) An antibiotic alone does not prevent tetanus.

PGI Exam Trap: A dressing alone is enough for this wound.

5-Second Recall: Clean the wound and give vaccine plus immunoglobulin.

PNC Exam Pearl: A dirty deep wound needs active and passive protection.

question: A nurse caring for the children of a village finds a high prevalence of night blindness among them. Which intervention is the MOST appropriate as the FIRST step?
option_1: Give a dose of vitamin A to the children and begin its regular rounds
option_2: Advise the families to give more green leafy vegetables at home
option_3: Test the eyes of all the children in the village school
option_4: Give the children iron and folic acid tablets each week
solution:
Correct Answer: (a) Give a dose of vitamin A to the children and begin its regular rounds

Clinical Rationale: Night blindness comes from a lack of vitamin A, so the FIRST step is to give a dose of vitamin A and to start the regular rounds of it.

Key Clue: night blindness among the children of a village

Priority Principle: Vitamin A deficiency

Why Not Others: (b) Diet advice helps but does not treat the present deficiency; (c) Eye testing finds the problem but does not treat it; (d) Iron and folic acid are for anaemia and not for night blindness.

PGI Exam Trap: Green leafy vegetables alone treat night blindness at once.

5-Second Recall: Give vitamin A and start its regular rounds.

PNC Exam Pearl: Night blindness means the child needs vitamin A.

question: A nurse caring for the adults of a village plans a programme to prevent coronary heart disease. Which measure is the MOST appropriate for primary prevention at the community level?
option_1: Referring the sick adults to the district hospital
option_2: Screening the adults for high blood pressure every year
option_3: Giving aspirin to the adults who have chest pain
option_4: Teaching the adults to stop smoking and to walk every day
solution:
Correct Answer: (d) Teaching the adults to stop smoking and to walk every day

Clinical Rationale: Primary prevention acts before the disease starts, so teaching the adults to stop smoking and to walk every day is the right community measure.

Key Clue: preventing coronary heart disease in the adults of a village

Priority Principle: Primary prevention

Why Not Others: (a) Referral is care for the sick and not prevention; (b) Screening finds early disease and belongs to secondary prevention; (c) Aspirin for chest pain is treatment and not prevention.

PGI Exam Trap: Screening the adults each year is primary prevention.

5-Second Recall: Stop smoking and walk daily to prevent disease.

PNC Exam Pearl: Prevention comes before the disease begins.

Reference Table: Normal adult vital signs - Temperature: 36.1-37.2 C (97-99 F); Pulse: 60-100 /min; Respiration: 12-20 /min; Blood pressure: < 120/80 mmHg; SpO2: 95-100% (COPD target 88-92%).

question: A nurse caring for a man who feels well after two months of treatment for tuberculosis explains why the full course is still completed. Which reason is the MOST appropriate?
option_1: The medicines are finished so that the stock is NOT wasted
option_2: The course is completed to keep the doctor happy
option_3: Stopping early lets the remaining bacteria grow back and become resistant
option_4: The full course gives him a stronger immunity for life
solution:
Correct Answer: (c) Stopping early lets the remaining bacteria grow back and become resistant

Clinical Rationale: Some bacteria survive after the man begins to feel well, so stopping early lets them grow back and become resistant to the drugs.

Key Clue: a man who feels well after two months of tuberculosis treatment

Priority Principle: Completing antitubercular therapy

Why Not Others: (a) Wasting the stock is not the reason for the full course; (b) Pleasing the doctor is not a reason based on the disease; (d) The course cures the disease and does not make him immune.

PGI Exam Trap: Stopping early makes no difference to the cure.

5-Second Recall: Finish the course to stop the bacteria returning.

PNC Exam Pearl: Feeling well does not mean the bacteria are gone.

question: A nurse caring for a man at the clinic is asked about the mode of transmission of the hepatitis B virus in the community. Which statement is the MOST appropriate?
option_1: It spreads through the bite of an infected mosquito
option_2: It spreads through drinking water and stale food
option_3: It spreads through the air when a person coughs
option_4: It spreads through blood and through sexual contact
solution:
Correct Answer: (d) It spreads through blood and through sexual contact

Clinical Rationale: The hepatitis B virus spreads through blood and through sexual contact and is NOT carried in water or food.

Key Clue: the mode of transmission of hepatitis B

Priority Principle: Hepatitis B

Why Not Others: (a) A mosquito bite does not carry hepatitis B; (b) Water and food carry hepatitis A and not hepatitis B; (c) Hepatitis B is not spread through the air by coughing.

PGI Exam Trap: Hepatitis B spreads through drinking water.

5-Second Recall: Blood and sexual contact carry the virus.

PNC Exam Pearl: Blood is the main road for hepatitis B.

question: A nurse caring for a child who has had one attack of rheumatic fever explains how a second attack can be prevented. Which measure is the MOST appropriate?
option_1: Give a regular monthly injection of long acting penicillin
option_2: Give a short course of penicillin for each sore throat
option_3: Keep the child at home during the cold season
option_4: Give aspirin daily to prevent the fever from coming
solution:
Correct Answer: (a) Give a regular monthly injection of long acting penicillin

Clinical Rationale: After one attack of rheumatic fever the child is given a regular monthly injection of long acting penicillin to prevent further attacks.

Key Clue: preventing a second attack of rheumatic fever

Priority Principle: Rheumatic fever prophylaxis

Why Not Others: (b) Treating each sore throat is not enough after a first attack; (c) Staying at home in the cold does not prevent the attack; (d) Daily aspirin does not prevent rheumatic fever.

PGI Exam Trap: A daily aspirin prevents the next attack.

5-Second Recall: A monthly penicillin injection prevents recurrence.

PNC Exam Pearl: Penicillin keeps the throat safe for the heart.

Reference Table: Normal adult vital signs - Temperature: 36.1-37.2 C (97-99 F); Pulse: 60-100 /min; Respiration: 12-20 /min; Blood pressure: < 120/80 mmHg; SpO2: 95-100% (COPD target 88-92%).

question: A nurse caring for a child in a village notes that 2000 school children were screened and 200 were found to have a refractive error. Which is the MOST appropriate prevalence of the refractive error?
option_1: 20 per cent
option_2: 10 per cent
option_3: 1 per cent
option_4: 5 per cent
solution:
Correct Answer: (b) 10 per cent

Clinical Rationale: Prevalence is the number of cases found among those examined, so 200 cases among 2000 children is a prevalence of 10 per cent.

Key Clue: 200 cases of refractive error among 2000 children screened

Priority Principle: Prevalence

Why Not Others: (a) 20 per cent would mean 400 cases among the 2000; (c) 1 per cent would mean only 20 cases among the 2000; (d) 5 per cent would mean 100 cases among the 2000.

PGI Exam Trap: The cases are multiplied by twenty to get the rate.

5-Second Recall: Divide the cases by the number screened.

PNC Exam Pearl: Prevalence is the share of the screened who have it.

question: A nurse caring for the children of a village gives health education before the immunisation session begins. Which reason for this order is the MOST appropriate?
option_1: It gives the staff time to arrange the vaccine vials
option_2: The children are calmer after listening to a short talk
option_3: The parents can then ask questions and give their consent before the vaccine
option_4: It is required by the rules of the immunisation programme
solution:
Correct Answer: (c) The parents can then ask questions and give their consent before the vaccine

Clinical Rationale: Health education before the session lets the parents ask their doubts and give their consent before the child is vaccinated.

Key Clue: health education before an immunisation session

Priority Principle: Health education

Why Not Others: (a) The staff arrange the vials in any case before the session; (b) A calmer child is a benefit and not the reason for the talk; (d) The value of the talk lies in consent and not in the rules.

PGI Exam Trap: The talk is given only because the rules ask for it.

5-Second Recall: Educate and answer the parents first.

PNC Exam Pearl: Informed parents give consent freely.

question: A nurse caring for a man with a suspected chest infection is to collect a sputum sample for examination. Which is the BEST order of the steps that the nurse should follow?
option_1: Collect the sample just after he takes a warm drink of milk
option_2: Collect the saliva from the mouth into the container
option_3: Ask him to spit after he swallows a small amount of water
option_4: Ask him to rinse the mouth, then cough out sputum into the container
solution:
Correct Answer: (d) Ask him to rinse the mouth, then cough out sputum into the container

Clinical Rationale: The mouth is rinsed FIRST and the man is then asked to cough out the sputum from deep in the chest straight into the container.

Key Clue: collecting a sputum sample from a man

Priority Principle: Sputum collection

Why Not Others: (a) A warm drink does not give a good sputum sample; (b) Saliva from the mouth is not sputum and gives a wrong report; (c) Spitting after water gives watery saliva and not sputum.

PGI Exam Trap: Mouth saliva is collected as the sputum sample.

5-Second Recall: Rinse the mouth, then cough out sputum.

PNC Exam Pearl: Sputum must come from the chest, not the mouth.

question: A nurse caring for a family in a village finds that the household is drinking untreated pond water. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Advise them to boil the water at once and explain the risk of disease
option_2: Ask the family to buy bottled water from the market
option_3: Report the family to the village health committee
option_4: Give them chlorine tablets and leave the house quietly
solution:
Correct Answer: (a) Advise them to boil the water at once and explain the risk of disease

Clinical Rationale: The FIRST step is to make the drinking water safe, so the family is told to boil the water at once and the risk of disease is explained.

Key Clue: a household drinking untreated pond water

Priority Principle: Safe drinking water

Why Not Others: (b) Bottled water is costly and not the first advice; (c) Reporting the family does not make the water safe; (d) Chlorine tablets help but the risk must be explained as well.

PGI Exam Trap: The family is reported to the village committee FIRST.

5-Second Recall: Make the water safe at once.

PNC Exam Pearl: Boiling is the first defence against water borne disease.

question: A pregnant woman with tuberculosis comes to the clinic for a check and now feels well. Which advice about her treatment is the MOST appropriate for the nurse to give?
option_1: Stop the treatment now as she feels well and the baby is safe
option_2: Continue the full course as advised and keep the regular check up
option_3: Take the drugs only on the days of the clinic visit
option_4: Wait until the delivery and then decide about the drugs
solution:
Correct Answer: (b) Continue the full course as advised and keep the regular check up

Clinical Rationale: A pregnant woman with tuberculosis must finish the full course, because feeling well does NOT mean that the disease is cured.

Key Clue: a pregnant woman with tuberculosis who feels well

Priority Principle: Tuberculosis in pregnancy

Why Not Others: (a) Stopping early lets the disease return and harm mother and baby; (c) The drugs are taken daily and not only on visit days; (d) Waiting for the delivery lets the disease progress.

PGI Exam Trap: The drugs are taken only on the clinic day.

5-Second Recall: Finish the full course as advised.

PNC Exam Pearl: Feeling well is not the same as being cured.

question: A nurse caring for an antenatal woman in a malaria area advises her to sleep under an insecticide treated net. Which reason is the MOST appropriate?
option_1: The net keeps away the houseflies from the sleeping place
option_2: The net keeps the room cool on hot and sticky nights
option_3: The net is given free and must be used by every family
option_4: The net protects her and the unborn baby from malaria and its harm
solution:
Correct Answer: (d) The net protects her and the unborn baby from malaria and its harm

Clinical Rationale: Malaria in pregnancy harms both the mother and the unborn baby, so an insecticide treated net is advised to protect them from the bite of the mosquito.

Key Clue: an antenatal woman in a malaria area

Priority Principle: Malaria in pregnancy

Why Not Others: (a) The net is meant for the mosquito and not the housefly; (b) Cooling the room is not the reason for using the net; (c) The net is given free, but protection is the real reason.

PGI Exam Trap: The net is used only to keep the houseflies away.

5-Second Recall: The net protects mother and baby from malaria.

PNC Exam Pearl: Malaria in pregnancy harms two lives.

question: A nurse caring for a family in a village reads that the community health card shows a sharp rise in acute respiratory infections in the winter months. Which interpretation is the MOST appropriate?
option_1: The rise shows that the vaccine programme of the area has failed
option_2: The card is filled wrongly as infection does NOT vary with season
option_3: The cases rise with the cold season and the service must plan for it
option_4: The rise means that the village water is unsafe for drinking
solution:
Correct Answer: (c) The cases rise with the cold season and the service must plan for it

Clinical Rationale: Acute respiratory infections rise in the cold months, so the card points to a seasonal increase that the service should plan for.

Key Clue: a rise in acute respiratory infections in winter

Priority Principle: Seasonal illness

Why Not Others: (a) The vaccine programme is not judged from these cases; (b) Respiratory infection does rise with the cold season; (d) Water does not explain this seasonal rise in the chest.

PGI Exam Trap: The rise is taken as a failure of the vaccine programme.

5-Second Recall: The rise is seasonal and needs planning.

PNC Exam Pearl: Cold months bring more chest infections.

question: A 1-year-old child with severe pneumonia is being referred to the district hospital. Which advice to the family during the transfer is the MOST appropriate?
option_1: Feed the child a full meal before starting the journey
option_2: Keep the child warm and give small sips of fluid on the way
option_3: Give the child a cough syrup to settle the breathing
option_4: Stop all fluids so that the child does NOT vomit
solution:
Correct Answer: (b) Keep the child warm and give small sips of fluid on the way

Clinical Rationale: During the transfer the child is kept warm and given small sips of fluid, so that the breathing is NOT made worse by cold or thirst.

Key Clue: a 1-year-old child with severe pneumonia in transfer

Priority Principle: Pneumonia referral

Why Not Others: (a) A full meal before the journey may cause vomiting and choking; (c) A cough syrup does not treat severe pneumonia; (d) Stopping the fluids dries the child and is harmful.

PGI Exam Trap: A cough syrup is given to settle the breathing.

5-Second Recall: Keep warm and give small sips.

PNC Exam Pearl: Warmth and fluid support the child in transfer.

question: A nurse caring for a family in a village is to disinfect a well after it is suspected to be contaminated. Which is the BEST order of the steps that the nurse should follow?
option_1: Find the volume of the water, then add the right amount of bleaching powder
option_2: Add the bleaching powder FIRST, then find the volume of water
option_3: Pour the powder into the well and then test the water
option_4: Empty the well completely and then fill it up again
solution:
Correct Answer: (a) Find the volume of the water, then add the right amount of bleaching powder

Clinical Rationale: The volume of water in the well is worked out FIRST, so that the right amount of bleaching powder is added.

Key Clue: disinfecting a well suspected to be contaminated

Priority Principle: Well disinfection

Why Not Others: (b) The powder cannot be measured before the water is measured; (c) Testing comes after the right dose is added and mixed; (d) Emptying and refilling the well is not the method used.

PGI Exam Trap: The powder is added before the water is measured.

5-Second Recall: Measure the water, then add the powder.

PNC Exam Pearl: The dose depends on the volume of water.

question: A nurse caring for a mother after delivery explains why breastfeeding is started within an hour of the birth. Which reason is the MOST appropriate?
option_1: It helps the mother to sleep well after the delivery
option_2: The baby is hungry and will cry until it is fed
option_3: It saves the nurse the work of feeding the baby later
option_4: The FIRST milk protects the baby and the suckling helps the uterus
solution:
Correct Answer: (d) The FIRST milk protects the baby and the suckling helps the uterus

Clinical Rationale: The FIRST milk is rich in protection for the baby and the act of suckling helps the uterus to contract after the birth.

Key Clue: starting breastfeeding within an hour of the birth

Priority Principle: Early breastfeeding

Why Not Others: (a) Helping the mother sleep is not the reason; (b) Hunger is not the reason for starting so early; (c) Saving the nurse work is not a reason for the practice.

PGI Exam Trap: Feeding is started early to help the mother sleep.

5-Second Recall: First milk protects and suckling contracts the uterus.

PNC Exam Pearl: The first hour gives the best milk and helps the womb.

question: A nurse caring for the children of a village finds that the families refuse the measles vaccine because of a rumour. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Talk with the community leaders to explain the facts about the vaccine
option_2: Report the families to the police for refusing the vaccine
option_3: Vaccinate the children quietly without telling the parents
option_4: Stop the session for the day and leave the whole village
solution:
Correct Answer: (a) Talk with the community leaders to explain the facts about the vaccine

Clinical Rationale: A rumour is BEST answered through the community leaders, so the nurse talks with them FIRST and explains the facts about the vaccine.

Key Clue: families refusing the measles vaccine after a rumour

Priority Principle: Vaccine hesitancy

Why Not Others: (b) The police do not settle a doubt about a vaccine; (c) Vaccinating without consent breaks the trust of the people; (d) Leaving the village leaves the children unprotected.

PGI Exam Trap: The children are vaccinated quietly without consent.

5-Second Recall: Explain the facts through the community leaders.

PNC Exam Pearl: Answer the rumour with the leaders of the village.

question: A nurse caring for a man in a factory notes that 50 of the 500 workers developed a skin allergy after a new chemical was introduced. Which is the MOST appropriate attack rate?
option_1: 1 per cent
option_2: 10 per cent
option_3: 20 per cent
option_4: 5 per cent
solution:
Correct Answer: (b) 10 per cent

Clinical Rationale: The attack rate is the number of new cases among those exposed, so 50 cases among 500 workers gives 10 per cent.

Key Clue: 50 cases of skin allergy among 500 workers

Priority Principle: Attack rate

Why Not Others: (a) 1 per cent would mean only five workers affected; (c) 20 per cent would mean a hundred workers affected; (d) 5 per cent would mean twenty five workers affected.

PGI Exam Trap: The cases are divided by a hundred to get the rate.

5-Second Recall: Divide the new cases by those exposed.

PNC Exam Pearl: The attack rate counts cases among the exposed.
