question: A mother of a newborn asks the nurse how many kilocalories per kilogram the baby needs each day. Which value is the MOST appropriate?
option_1: About 200 kilocalories per kilogram each day
option_2: About 60 kilocalories per kilogram each day
option_3: About 120 kilocalories per kilogram each day
option_4: About 20 kilocalories per kilogram each day
solution:
Correct Answer: (c) About 120 kilocalories per kilogram each day

Clinical Rationale: A newborn needs about 120 kilocalories for every kilogram of body weight each day for normal growth.

Key Clue: the kilocalories a newborn needs each day

Priority Principle: Newborn nutrition

Why Not Others: (a) A value of 200 is far too high for a newborn; (b) A value of 60 is only about half of the daily need; (d) A value of 20 is far too low for a newborn.

PGI Exam Trap: A value of 60 kilocalories is the daily need.

5-Second Recall: About 120 kilocalories for each kilogram.

PNC Exam Pearl: A newborn needs about 120 kcal/kg/day.

question: A nurse caring for a mother of a low birth weight baby explains why kangaroo mother care is promoted at the community level. Which reason is the MOST appropriate?
option_1: It saves the family the cost of buying warm clothes
option_2: Skin to skin warmth keeps the baby warm and helps feeding and weight gain
option_3: It keeps the baby away from the other members of the family
option_4: It is a tradition that the family wants to follow at home
solution:
Correct Answer: (b) Skin to skin warmth keeps the baby warm and helps feeding and weight gain

Clinical Rationale: Kangaroo mother care keeps the baby warm against the mother's skin and so helps feeding and steady weight gain.

Key Clue: kangaroo mother care for a low birth weight baby

Priority Principle: Kangaroo mother care

Why Not Others: (a) Saving the cost of clothes is not the health reason; (c) The method brings the baby close and does not keep it away; (d) It is a health practice and not a family tradition.

PGI Exam Trap: The method is used to save the cost of warm clothes.

5-Second Recall: Skin to skin warmth helps feeding and growth.

PNC Exam Pearl: The mother's skin is the cheapest warmer.

question: A nurse caring for a man on treatment for tuberculosis explains why directly observed treatment is followed for him. Which reason is the MOST appropriate?
option_1: A health worker watches him take the drugs so the course is completed
option_2: It saves the patient the cost of buying the drugs
option_3: It keeps the patient away from the other people at home
option_4: It moves the treatment from the clinic to the home
solution:
Correct Answer: (a) A health worker watches him take the drugs so the course is completed

Clinical Rationale: In directly observed treatment a health worker watches the patient swallow the drugs, so the full course is taken and the disease is cured.

Key Clue: directly observed treatment for tuberculosis

Priority Principle: Directly observed treatment

Why Not Others: (b) The drugs are free in any case and cost is not the reason; (c) The method does not separate the patient from the family; (d) The place of treatment is not the reason for the method.

PGI Exam Trap: The method is followed to save the cost of the drugs.

5-Second Recall: Watching him take the drugs completes the course.

PNC Exam Pearl: Seen doses cure the disease faster.

question: A nurse caring for a family in a village is offered a gift by the family to give them extra services. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Refuse the gift and report the family to the police
option_2: Accept the gift and give the family the extra services
option_3: Accept the gift and share it with the other staff members
option_4: Decline the gift politely and explain the rule of equal service to all
solution:
Correct Answer: (d) Decline the gift politely and explain the rule of equal service to all

Clinical Rationale: A nurse serves every family equally, so the gift is politely declined and the rule of equal service is explained to the family.

Key Clue: a family offering a gift for extra services

Priority Principle: Ethical practice

Why Not Others: (a) Reporting the family to the police is far too harsh; (b) Accepting the gift for extra service is unfair to the others; (c) Sharing the gift still amounts to taking the gift.

PGI Exam Trap: The gift is accepted and the extra service is given.

5-Second Recall: Decline the gift and serve all equally.

PNC Exam Pearl: A gift must not change the care given.

question: A nurse caring for an adolescent girl at the school gives her iron and folic acid tablets. Which counselling point is the MOST appropriate?
option_1: Take the tablet when she feels weak or tired
option_2: Take the tablet on an empty stomach with strong tea
option_3: Take the tablet after food and avoid tea or coffee with it
option_4: Take all the tablets for the week on a single day
solution:
Correct Answer: (c) Take the tablet after food and avoid tea or coffee with it

Clinical Rationale: Iron is taken after food to prevent stomach upset, and tea or coffee is avoided because it reduces the absorption of the iron.

Key Clue: giving iron and folic acid to an adolescent girl

Priority Principle: Iron and folic acid

Why Not Others: (a) The tablet is taken regularly and not by how she feels; (b) Strong tea lowers the absorption and upsets the stomach; (d) Taking the whole week at once is harmful and not advised.

PGI Exam Trap: The tablet is taken on an empty stomach with strong tea.

5-Second Recall: Take it after food and avoid tea with it.

PNC Exam Pearl: Tea blocks the iron taken by the girl.

question: A nurse caring for a woman at the clinic explains why the body temperature rises slightly in the second half of the menstrual cycle. Which reason is the MOST appropriate?
option_1: The woman eats a little more food during these days
option_2: The uterus becomes warm as it prepares for pregnancy
option_3: The hormone progesterone acts on the heat regulating centre
option_4: The blood flow to the skin is reduced at this time
solution:
Correct Answer: (c) The hormone progesterone acts on the heat regulating centre

Clinical Rationale: After ovulation the level of progesterone rises and acts on the heat regulating centre, so the body temperature rises slightly.

Key Clue: a slight rise of temperature in the second half of the cycle

Priority Principle: Menstrual cycle

Why Not Others: (a) The food eaten does not explain this fixed rise; (b) The uterus does not warm the whole body in this way; (d) The skin blood flow does not cause the rise.

PGI Exam Trap: The uterus warms the body to raise the temperature.

5-Second Recall: Progesterone lifts the temperature after ovulation.

PNC Exam Pearl: The cycle nudges the thermostat up.

Reference Table: Normal adult vital signs - Temperature: 36.1-37.2 C (97-99 F); Pulse: 60-100 /min; Respiration: 12-20 /min; Blood pressure: < 120/80 mmHg; SpO2: 95-100% (COPD target 88-92%).

question: A nurse caring for a family in a village is asked what the letters ORS stand for in the child health programme. Which answer is the MOST appropriate?
option_1: Oral routine supplement
option_2: Oral rehydration solution
option_3: Oral rehydration syrup
option_4: Ordinary rehydration salts
solution:
Correct Answer: (b) Oral rehydration solution

Clinical Rationale: The letters ORS stand for oral rehydration solution, the fluid given to a child with diarrhoea to replace the lost water and salts.

Key Clue: the full form of ORS in the child programme

Priority Principle: Oral rehydration solution

Why Not Others: (a) A routine supplement is a different thing altogether; (c) Syrup is not what the letters ORS stand for; (d) The word ordinary does not belong in the full form.

PGI Exam Trap: The letters stand for oral routine supplement.

5-Second Recall: ORS means oral rehydration solution.

PNC Exam Pearl: ORS replaces water and salts by mouth.

question: A nurse caring for a man who works in a battery factory finds that his blood lead level is raised on screening. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Remove him from the lead exposure and send him for treatment
option_2: Advise him to wear a mask and continue the same work
option_3: Repeat the blood test after one month from now
option_4: Give him iron tablets to bring the lead level down
solution:
Correct Answer: (a) Remove him from the lead exposure and send him for treatment

Clinical Rationale: The FIRST step in lead poisoning is to stop the exposure, so he is removed from the lead and sent for treatment.

Key Clue: a raised blood lead level in a factory worker

Priority Principle: Lead poisoning

Why Not Others: (b) A mask alone does not stop the lead from entering the body; (c) Repeating the test later leaves him exposed for a month; (d) Iron tablets do not treat a raised lead level.

PGI Exam Trap: A mask is enough for him to continue the same work.

5-Second Recall: Stop the exposure and start treatment.

PNC Exam Pearl: First remove the poison, then treat the man.

question: A nurse caring for a newborn on the ward explains which drug is given as a single dose to the eyes to prevent infection from the mother. Which drug is the MOST appropriate?
option_1: Normal saline eye drops
option_2: Chloramphenicol eye drops
option_3: Silver nitrate eye drops
option_4: Erythromycin eye ointment
solution:
Correct Answer: (d) Erythromycin eye ointment

Clinical Rationale: A single dose of erythromycin eye ointment is put into the eyes of the newborn to prevent the eye infection that may come from the mother.

Key Clue: a single dose of a drug for the eyes of a newborn

Priority Principle: Newborn eye care

Why Not Others: (a) Normal saline cleans the eye but does not prevent infection; (b) Chloramphenicol drops are not the drug used at birth; (c) Silver nitrate is no longer the drug of choice here.

PGI Exam Trap: Normal saline is put in the eyes to prevent infection.

5-Second Recall: Erythromycin ointment protects the newborn eyes.

PNC Exam Pearl: One dose of ointment guards the eyes at birth.

question: A nurse caring for a pregnant woman at the anganwadi explains why supplementary nutrition is given to her. Which reason is the MOST appropriate?
option_1: It saves the family the cost of buying food at home
option_2: It meets the extra needs of pregnancy and helps the baby to grow well
option_3: It is given so that the mother gains a lot of weight quickly
option_4: It is a free supply that every woman must collect from the centre
solution:
Correct Answer: (b) It meets the extra needs of pregnancy and helps the baby to grow well

Clinical Rationale: Pregnancy raises the need for food and nutrients, so the supplementary nutrition meets this extra need and helps the baby to grow well.

Key Clue: supplementary nutrition for a pregnant woman at the anganwadi

Priority Principle: Supplementary nutrition

Why Not Others: (a) Saving the cost is a benefit and not the health reason; (c) Rapid weight gain is not the aim of the supplement; (d) It is given for health and not because it is free.

PGI Exam Trap: The supplement is given mainly to save the family money.

5-Second Recall: It meets the extra needs of pregnancy.

PNC Exam Pearl: Pregnancy needs more food and nutrients.

question: A nurse caring for a child at the cold chain point explains which vaccine is kept in the freezer at the top of the cold chain. Which vaccine is the MOST appropriate?
option_1: The oral polio vaccine
option_2: The measles vaccine
option_3: The BCG vaccine
option_4: The DPT vaccine
solution:
Correct Answer: (a) The oral polio vaccine

Clinical Rationale: The oral polio vaccine is stored in the freezer at the top of the cold chain because it is damaged by heat.

Key Clue: the vaccine stored in the freezer of the cold chain

Priority Principle: Cold chain

Why Not Others: (b) The measles vaccine is kept cold but not in the freezer; (c) The BCG vaccine is kept cold and is not frozen; (d) The DPT vaccine must never be frozen at all.

PGI Exam Trap: The measles vaccine is kept in the freezer.

5-Second Recall: The oral polio vaccine is stored frozen.

PNC Exam Pearl: OPV lives in the freezer; DPT must not.

question: A nurse caring for a family in a district is asked how the neonatal mortality rate is defined. Which statement is the BEST definition of the neonatal mortality rate?
option_1: Deaths of newborns on the FIRST day per 1000 live births
option_2: Deaths of newborns within the FIRST 7 days per 1000 live births
option_3: Deaths of infants under one year per 1000 live births
option_4: Deaths of newborns within the FIRST 28 days per 1000 live births
solution:
Correct Answer: (d) Deaths of newborns within the FIRST 28 days per 1000 live births

Clinical Rationale: The neonatal mortality rate counts the deaths of babies in the FIRST 28 days of life for every 1000 live births in a year.

Key Clue: the definition of the neonatal mortality rate

Priority Principle: Neonatal mortality rate

Why Not Others: (a) Deaths on the first day are a part of the whole 28 days; (b) Deaths in the first week give the early neonatal rate; (c) Deaths under one year give the infant mortality rate.

PGI Exam Trap: Deaths in the FIRST week give the neonatal rate.

5-Second Recall: First 28 days of life per 1000 live births.

PNC Exam Pearl: Neonatal means the first four weeks.

question: A nurse caring for a pregnant woman explains why the blood volume increases by about forty per cent in pregnancy. Which reason is the MOST appropriate?
option_1: It prepares the mother for the loss of blood at delivery
option_2: It thins the blood so that it flows more easily in the body
option_3: It meets the needs of the growing fetus and of the uterus and placenta
option_4: It raises the blood pressure of the mother during pregnancy
solution:
Correct Answer: (c) It meets the needs of the growing fetus and of the uterus and placenta

Clinical Rationale: The blood volume rises to supply the growing fetus and the enlarged uterus and placenta, which need a large flow of blood.

Key Clue: a rise of blood volume by forty per cent in pregnancy

Priority Principle: Blood volume in pregnancy

Why Not Others: (a) Some extra blood does help at delivery, but the needs of the fetus are the main reason; (b) Easier flow is a result and not the reason for the rise; (d) The blood pressure does not rise because of the extra volume.

PGI Exam Trap: The extra blood is there to raise the blood pressure.

5-Second Recall: The fetus and uterus need the extra blood.

PNC Exam Pearl: Pregnancy builds a bigger blood supply for two.

Reference Table: Normal adult vital signs - Temperature: 36.1-37.2 C (97-99 F); Pulse: 60-100 /min; Respiration: 12-20 /min; Blood pressure: < 120/80 mmHg; SpO2: 95-100% (COPD target 88-92%).

question: A nurse caring for a family in a village explains why the registration of a birth is important. Which reason is the MOST appropriate?
option_1: It helps the family to get a free gift for the child
option_2: It gives the child a legal identity and a record for the health services
option_3: It is done when the child is taken for a vaccine
option_4: It is needed to decide the number of houses to build
solution:
Correct Answer: (b) It gives the child a legal identity and a record for the health services

Clinical Rationale: The registration of a birth gives the child a legal identity and a record that the health services can use to plan the care of the child.

Key Clue: the registration of a birth in a village

Priority Principle: Birth registration

Why Not Others: (a) A free gift is not the purpose of registering a birth; (c) The registration is a right of the child and not tied to a vaccine; (d) Houses are not planned from the birth register.

PGI Exam Trap: The birth is registered to get a free gift for the child.

5-Second Recall: Registration gives the child a legal identity.

PNC Exam Pearl: A registered child exists in law and in care.

question: A nurse caring for a child at the anganwadi finds the weight for age in the red zone of the growth chart. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Weigh the child again on the next visit to confirm the finding
option_2: Send the child home and review the weight after three months
option_3: Assess the child for illness and start feeding advice and follow up
option_4: Give the family a chart and ask them to fill it up at home
solution:
Correct Answer: (c) Assess the child for illness and start feeding advice and follow up

Clinical Rationale: A weight for age in the red zone means severe undernutrition, so the child is checked for illness and feeding advice and follow up are started at once.

Key Clue: a weight for age in the red zone of the growth chart

Priority Principle: Severe undernutrition

Why Not Others: (a) Waiting for the next visit delays the care that is needed; (b) A review after three months is far too late for this child; (d) A home chart does not treat the severe undernutrition.

PGI Exam Trap: The child is sent home and reviewed after three months.

5-Second Recall: Check for illness and begin feeding advice.

PNC Exam Pearl: The red zone needs action today.

question: A nurse caring for the family of a man with cholera explains which drug is given to the whole family as chemoprophylaxis when it is advised. Which drug is the MOST appropriate?
option_1: Cotrimoxazole for seven days
option_2: Metronidazole for five days
option_3: Ampicillin for three days
option_4: Doxycycline as a single dose
solution:
Correct Answer: (d) Doxycycline as a single dose

Clinical Rationale: A single dose of doxycycline is given to the close contacts of a case of cholera as chemoprophylaxis when it is advised.

Key Clue: a single dose of a drug for the family of a cholera case

Priority Principle: Cholera chemoprophylaxis

Why Not Others: (a) Cotrimoxazole is not the drug for cholera contacts; (b) Metronidazole is not the drug used for cholera contacts; (c) Ampicillin is not given as the single dose here.

PGI Exam Trap: Metronidazole is given to the family of a cholera case.

5-Second Recall: Doxycycline as a single dose for contacts.

PNC Exam Pearl: A single dose protects the family of a cholera case.

question: A nurse caring for a newborn on the ward notes that the birth weight is 2.4 kilograms. Which is the MOST appropriate classification of this baby?
option_1: Low birth weight
option_2: Normal birth weight
option_3: Very low birth weight
option_4: Macrosomia
solution:
Correct Answer: (a) Low birth weight

Clinical Rationale: A baby who weighs less than 2.5 kilograms at birth is classed as low birth weight.

Key Clue: a birth weight of 2.4 kilograms

Priority Principle: Birth weight classification

Why Not Others: (b) A normal birth weight is 2.5 kilograms or more; (c) Very low birth weight is below 1.5 kilograms; (d) Macrosomia means a very large baby and not this weight.

PGI Exam Trap: A weight of 2.4 kilograms is called normal.

5-Second Recall: Below 2.5 kilograms is low birth weight.

PNC Exam Pearl: The 2.5 kilogram line divides low from normal.

question: A nurse caring for the children of a village explains which group is the target for the vitamin A prophylaxis under the national programme. Which group is the MOST appropriate?
option_1: Children from nine months to five years of age
option_2: Children from birth to nine months of age
option_3: All the school children up to twelve years
option_4: The pregnant women of the whole village
solution:
Correct Answer: (a) Children from nine months to five years of age

Clinical Rationale: Under the national programme vitamin A is given to the children from nine months up to five years of age.

Key Clue: the target group for the vitamin A prophylaxis

Priority Principle: Vitamin A programme

Why Not Others: (b) The dose begins at nine months and not from birth; (c) The programme targets the under fives and not all school children; (d) The pregnant women are not the target group for this dose.

PGI Exam Trap: The dose is given to all the school children.

5-Second Recall: Vitamin A is for children of nine months to five years.

PNC Exam Pearl: The under fives are the target of the dose.

question: A nurse caring for a pregnant woman explains why the basal metabolic rate rises in pregnancy. Which reason is the MOST appropriate?
option_1: The mother eats a great deal more food in the whole pregnancy
option_2: The growing fetus and the placenta use up the extra energy of the mother
option_3: The body of the mother works harder to keep itself warm
option_4: The uterus contracts often and uses up the extra energy
solution:
Correct Answer: (b) The growing fetus and the placenta use up the extra energy of the mother

Clinical Rationale: The basal metabolic rate rises because the growing fetus, the uterus and the placenta need the extra energy of the mother.

Key Clue: a rise of the basal metabolic rate in pregnancy

Priority Principle: Metabolic rate in pregnancy

Why Not Others: (a) More food eaten is a result and not the cause of the rise; (c) Keeping warm does not explain this rise in metabolism; (d) The uterus does not contract enough to raise the rate so much.

PGI Exam Trap: The rate rises mainly to keep the mother warm.

5-Second Recall: The fetus and placenta need the extra energy.

PNC Exam Pearl: Two bodies raise the mother's furnace.

question: A nurse caring for a family in a village finds an abandoned infant near the bus stop. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Leave the infant with a neighbour and go on with the work
option_2: Take the infant home and look after it till the morning
option_3: Keep the infant warm and safe and inform the police and the health officer
option_4: Give the infant a feed of milk and wait for the mother
solution:
Correct Answer: (c) Keep the infant warm and safe and inform the police and the health officer

Clinical Rationale: An abandoned infant is at risk, so the nurse FIRST keeps the baby warm and safe and informs the police and the health officer at once.

Key Clue: an abandoned infant found near the bus stop

Priority Principle: Abandoned infant

Why Not Others: (a) Leaving the baby with a neighbour is not the proper step; (b) Taking the baby home is not a safe legal arrangement; (d) Waiting for the mother leaves the baby unsafe.

PGI Exam Trap: The nurse takes the infant home for the night.

5-Second Recall: Keep it warm and inform the police at once.

PNC Exam Pearl: An abandoned baby needs safety and the law.

question: A nurse caring for a mother after a home delivery plans a follow up visit within a week. Which reason for this visit is the MOST appropriate?
option_1: To take back the bag and the articles used in the delivery
option_2: To collect the money for the services that were given
option_3: To give the family the birth certificate of the baby
option_4: To check the mother and the baby for danger signs at an early stage
solution:
Correct Answer: (d) To check the mother and the baby for danger signs at an early stage

Clinical Rationale: The early follow up visit checks the mother and the newborn for danger signs before any problem becomes serious.

Key Clue: a follow up home visit within a week of delivery

Priority Principle: Postnatal follow up

Why Not Others: (a) The bag and the articles are not the reason for the visit; (b) Collecting money is not the purpose of the follow up visit; (c) The birth certificate is not given at this visit.

PGI Exam Trap: The visit is made to collect the delivery charges.

5-Second Recall: Check mother and baby for danger signs.

PNC Exam Pearl: An early check catches danger signs.

question: A nurse caring for a man at the clinic is asked about the mode of transmission of rabies to a human. Which statement is the MOST appropriate?
option_1: It spreads through the bite or the scratch of an infected animal
option_2: It spreads through the drinking water of the village
option_3: It spreads through the air from one person to another
option_4: It spreads through the bite of an infected mosquito
solution:
Correct Answer: (a) It spreads through the bite or the scratch of an infected animal

Clinical Rationale: Rabies spreads to a human through the bite or the scratch of an infected animal such as a dog.

Key Clue: the mode of transmission of rabies to a human

Priority Principle: Rabies

Why Not Others: (b) Rabies is not carried in the drinking water; (c) Rabies does not spread through the air between people; (d) A mosquito bite does not carry rabies.

PGI Exam Trap: Rabies spreads through the air from person to person.

5-Second Recall: The bite of an infected animal carries rabies.

PNC Exam Pearl: Rabies travels in the saliva of the bite.

question: A nurse caring for an adolescent girl in a village gives her a weekly iron and folic acid tablet. Which counselling point is the MOST appropriate?
option_1: Take the tablet when she has her monthly period
option_2: Take the tablet every morning on an empty stomach
option_3: Take two tablets in a week to make up for a missed one
option_4: Take the tablet on the same day every week after a meal
solution:
Correct Answer: (d) Take the tablet on the same day every week after a meal

Clinical Rationale: The weekly iron and folic acid tablet is taken on the same day each week after a meal, so that the stomach is NOT upset and the habit is kept.

Key Clue: a weekly iron and folic acid tablet for an adolescent girl

Priority Principle: Weekly iron and folic acid

Why Not Others: (a) It is taken every week and not just during the period; (b) The weekly tablet is taken after food and not on an empty stomach; (c) Two tablets together are not taken to make up for a missed one.

PGI Exam Trap: Two tablets are taken together to make up a missed dose.

5-Second Recall: Take it on the same day each week after food.

PNC Exam Pearl: One tablet, same day, every week.

question: A nurse caring for a family in a village explains why the knowledge of the local beliefs is important for the community health nurse. Which reason is the MOST appropriate?
option_1: It gives the nurse something to talk about during the visit
option_2: It helps the nurse to change the beliefs of the people at once
option_3: It helps the nurse to plan care that the people accept and follow
option_4: It is needed to write the yearly report of the area
solution:
Correct Answer: (c) It helps the nurse to plan care that the people accept and follow

Clinical Rationale: Knowing the local beliefs helps the nurse to plan care in a way that the people accept and follow in their daily life.

Key Clue: why the local beliefs matter to the community health nurse

Priority Principle: Culture and health

Why Not Others: (a) A topic of talk is not the reason for studying beliefs; (b) Beliefs are not changed at once and this is not the purpose; (d) The yearly report does not need the local beliefs.

PGI Exam Trap: The beliefs are studied to change them at once.

5-Second Recall: Local beliefs help the care to be accepted.

PNC Exam Pearl: Care that fits the beliefs is carried out.

question: A nurse caring for a man on treatment for tuberculosis explains why a follow up system is kept for the defaulters. Which reason is the MOST appropriate?
option_1: The defaulters are fined for missing the dose at the centre
option_2: The defaulters are traced and brought back so their treatment is finished
option_3: The names are kept so that the reports look complete
option_4: The defaulters are sent away from the treatment centre
solution:
Correct Answer: (b) The defaulters are traced and brought back so their treatment is finished

Clinical Rationale: A defaulter who misses the treatment is traced and brought back, so that the full course is completed and the cure is NOT lost.

Key Clue: a follow up system for the defaulters of treatment

Priority Principle: Defaulter tracing

Why Not Others: (a) A fine does not bring the patient back to the treatment; (c) Complete reports are not the reason for the follow up; (d) Sending the patient away loses the cure and spreads the disease.

PGI Exam Trap: The defaulter is fined for missing the dose.

5-Second Recall: Trace the defaulter and finish the course.

PNC Exam Pearl: A missed dose is chased, not punished.

question: A nurse caring for a child in a village school is asked which preventable cause of deafness is the MOST common among the children. Which cause is the MOST appropriate explanation?
option_1: Exposure to very loud noise in the home
option_2: A birth injury to the head during the delivery
option_3: A long standing infection of the ear that was NOT treated
option_4: Inheritance from the parents of the child
solution:
Correct Answer: (c) A long standing infection of the ear that was NOT treated

Clinical Rationale: A long standing infection of the middle ear that is NOT treated is the MOST common preventable cause of deafness in children.

Key Clue: deafness in the children of a village

Priority Principle: Preventable deafness

Why Not Others: (a) Loud noise at home is not the common cause in children; (b) A birth injury is much less common than an ear infection; (d) Inheritance is not the common preventable cause here.

PGI Exam Trap: Deafness in these children is inherited mainly.

5-Second Recall: An untreated ear infection is the common cause.

PNC Exam Pearl: An untreated ear infection steals hearing.

question: A nurse caring for the children of a village school is to conduct a school health check up. Which is the BEST order of the steps that the nurse should follow?
option_1: Refer the children FIRST, then screen and record them
option_2: Screen the children FIRST, then plan, then record the findings
option_3: Record the children FIRST, then screen and refer them
option_4: Plan with the teachers, screen the children, then record and refer
solution:
Correct Answer: (d) Plan with the teachers, screen the children, then record and refer

Clinical Rationale: A school health check up is planned with the teachers, the children are then screened, and the findings are recorded and referred.

Key Clue: a school health check up in a village school

Priority Principle: School health check up

Why Not Others: (a) A referral comes after the screening and not before it; (b) Screening before planning with the teachers is not the order; (c) Children cannot be recorded before they are screened.

PGI Exam Trap: The children are referred before they are screened.

5-Second Recall: Plan, screen, then record and refer.

PNC Exam Pearl: Plan with the school before the screening.

question: A nurse caring for a family in a village explains the method to dispose of the solid waste of the household. Which method is the MOST appropriate?
option_1: Bury the waste in a pit away from the source of water
option_2: Throw the waste into the river that runs near the village
option_3: Burn all the waste in an open place every day
option_4: Leave the waste in a heap behind the house
solution:
Correct Answer: (a) Bury the waste in a pit away from the source of water

Clinical Rationale: The household waste is BEST buried in a pit that is kept away from the source of drinking water, so that the flies and the water are NOT contaminated.

Key Clue: the disposal of household solid waste in a village

Priority Principle: Solid waste disposal

Why Not Others: (b) Throwing the waste in the river spoils the water supply; (c) Burning all the waste pollutes the air of the village; (d) A heap behind the house breeds flies and rats.

PGI Exam Trap: The waste is thrown into the river each day.

5-Second Recall: Bury the waste away from the water source.

PNC Exam Pearl: A pit keeps the waste from the water.

question: A nurse caring for a newborn on the unit plans a measure to prevent infection in the special care nursery. Which measure is the MOST appropriate?
option_1: Keep all the babies together in one large room
option_2: Wash the hands before and after touching every baby
option_3: Change the bed sheets once in a week
option_4: Allow the visitors to hold the babies freely
solution:
Correct Answer: (b) Wash the hands before and after touching every baby

Clinical Rationale: Hand washing before and after touching every baby is the single MOST useful measure to prevent infection in a nursery.

Key Clue: preventing infection in a special care nursery

Priority Principle: Hospital infection control

Why Not Others: (a) Keeping all the babies together spreads the infection faster; (c) A weekly change of sheets is far too seldom for a nursery; (d) Unrestricted visitors bring infection to the babies.

PGI Exam Trap: The babies are kept together in one large room.

5-Second Recall: Wash hands before and after each baby.

PNC Exam Pearl: Clean hands are the best guard in a nursery.

question: A nurse caring for a mother whose one year old child is brought for the second dose of the measles vaccine. Which advice to the mother is the MOST appropriate?
option_1: The child may get a mild fever or rash for a day or two after the dose
option_2: The child must be kept at home for a whole week afterwards
option_3: The child should NOT be bathed for at least three days
option_4: The child will NOT get measles after this one dose
solution:
Correct Answer: (a) The child may get a mild fever or rash for a day or two after the dose

Clinical Rationale: A mild fever or a rash for a day or two may follow the measles vaccine and is NOT a cause for worry, so the mother is told about it.

Key Clue: the second dose of the measles vaccine for a one year old child

Priority Principle: Measles vaccine

Why Not Others: (b) Keeping the child at home for a week is not needed; (c) There is no need to stop the bath after the vaccine; (d) The child is protected but is not said to be certain never.

PGI Exam Trap: The child must be kept at home for a whole week.

5-Second Recall: A mild fever or rash may follow the dose.

PNC Exam Pearl: Mild fever after the vaccine is normal.

question: A nurse caring for a woman with anaemia explains why iron is given together with folic acid in the anaemia programme. Which reason is the MOST appropriate?
option_1: The folic acid helps the stomach to take in the iron well
option_2: Both of them are needed to build healthy red blood cells
option_3: The iron protects the body from the side effects of the folic acid
option_4: The two together act faster than the iron given on its own
solution:
Correct Answer: (b) Both of them are needed to build healthy red blood cells

Clinical Rationale: Iron and folic acid are both needed for the making of healthy red blood cells, so they are given together in the anaemia programme.

Key Clue: giving iron along with folic acid for anaemia

Priority Principle: Anaemia programme

Why Not Others: (a) The folic acid is not given to improve the absorption of iron; (c) The iron does not act against the side effects of folic acid; (d) The two are given because both are needed and not for speed.

PGI Exam Trap: The folic acid is given to help absorb the iron.

5-Second Recall: Both are needed to build red blood cells.

PNC Exam Pearl: Two nutrients build one red cell.

question: A nurse caring for a family in a village is to notify an infectious disease at the sub centre. Which is the BEST order of the steps that the nurse should follow?
option_1: Fill the form and then wait to see more such cases
option_2: Send the form FIRST, then confirm the case and fill it
option_3: Confirm the case, fill the form, then send it to the health officer
option_4: Inform the neighbours FIRST and then write the form
solution:
Correct Answer: (c) Confirm the case, fill the form, then send it to the health officer

Clinical Rationale: For the notification of an infectious disease the case is confirmed, the form is filled, and it is then sent to the health officer.

Key Clue: the notification of an infectious disease at the sub centre

Priority Principle: Notification of disease

Why Not Others: (a) Waiting for more cases delays the whole notification; (b) An unconfirmed case cannot be sent on the form; (d) Informing the neighbours does not replace the notification.

PGI Exam Trap: The form is sent before the case is confirmed.

5-Second Recall: Confirm, fill the form, then send it.

PNC Exam Pearl: Confirm first, report second.

question: A nurse caring for a family in a village is asked which level of the health care pyramid the community health nurse of a sub centre works at. Which level is the MOST appropriate?
option_1: The district level of health care
option_2: The secondary level of health care
option_3: The tertiary level of health care
option_4: The primary level of health care
solution:
Correct Answer: (d) The primary level of health care

Clinical Rationale: The community health nurse of a sub centre works at the primary level, which is the base of the health care pyramid.

Key Clue: the level of the health care pyramid for a sub centre nurse

Priority Principle: Health care pyramid

Why Not Others: (a) The district level is above the primary and not the sub centre; (b) The secondary level is the district hospital and not the sub centre; (c) The tertiary level is the medical college and not the sub centre.

PGI Exam Trap: The sub centre nurse works at the secondary level.

5-Second Recall: The sub centre nurse works at the primary level.

PNC Exam Pearl: The sub centre sits at the base of the pyramid.
